content: <thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the most plausible molecular formula for the compound is C5H10O7 (neutral mass ≈ 182.04 Da, giving an [M+H]⁺ ion at m/z ≈ 183.05). This formula fits the observed isotopic pattern (small M+1 peak) and the exact mass of the base peak. The corresponding SMILES for a pentose‑type aldonic acid with an extra hydroxyl group (e.g., a dihydroxy‑pentanoic acid) is **OC(=O)C(O)C(O)C(O)CO**. This SMILES string represents a five‑carbon chain bearing a carboxylic acid and four hydroxyl groups, matching the formula C5H10O7.
